long_biography.plain_text:
At Incat’s Hobart shipyard, Craig Clifford oversees the commercial side of building aluminium ferries for customers around the world. His work spans international sales, chartering and the long-cycle negotiations needed to turn large export contracts into delivered vessels. He has also represented the sector through the Australian Shipbuilders Association.

Clifford now helps guide Incat’s move into battery-electric and hybrid propulsion. He has served as Denmark’s honorary consul in Tasmania since 2016, a public role connected to the state’s international relationships. Competitive sailing is another enduring commitment: he crewed on the line-honours winner of the 1994 Sydney to Hobart race and later returned to international offshore competition.

At Incat’s Hobart shipyard, Craig Clifford oversees the commercial side of building aluminium ferries for customers around the world. His work spans international sales, chartering and the long-cycle negotiations needed to turn large export contracts into delivered vessels. He has also represented the sector through the Australian Shipbuilders Association.

Clifford now helps guide Incat’s move into battery-electric and hybrid propulsion. He has served as Denmark’s honorary consul in Tasmania since 2016, a public role connected to the state’s international relationships. Competitive sailing is another enduring commitment: he crewed on the line-honours winner of the 1994 Sydney to Hobart race and later returned to international offshore competition.
